title: Onprem release orchestration validation playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a pragmatic playbook for verifying on-prem / VPC private-deploy releases end-to-end. Focus: CI/CD pipelines (GitOps/Argo/Helm), image signing and attestation, Terraform module interactions, and automated validation steps to reduce human rollback mistakes.

Audience:
- Release engineers and SREs supporting private clusters
- Solutions engineers running customer upgrades
- Build/infra authors who maintain charts and TF modules

Non-goals:
- Full security hardening checklist (see security-and-compliance space)
- Exhaustive smoke test definitions per customer (these live in the customer repo)

Quick glossary:
- control-plane repo: repo that holds Argo Application YAMLs / kustomize overlays
- artifact-bundle: OCI bundle produced by the release pipeline (images + chart tgz + SBOM + attestations)
- signer: cosign/HSM entity that signs container images and Helm charts

Pre-release checklist (automatable gates):
1) CI artifacts produced and uploaded
   - images pushed to customer registry mirror or staging registry with immutable tags (sha256)
   - chart tarball created with Chart.yaml version bumped (semver)
   - SBOM generated for each image (syft) and attached to bundle
   - cosign signatures and attestation files attached to bundle (see Signing section)
2) Terraform plan run and reviewed
   - TF modules that alter cluster IAM, registry access, or operator privileges must have a plan link in PR
   - Ops owner acknowledges drift risks (comment with link INF-xxxx)
3) Argo manifests validated locally
   - argocd app manifests pass schema check (argocd-util validate)
   - kustomize build completes for all overlays
4) Canary acceptance plan written and linked to release PR

Signing and provenance (practical notes):
- We require cosign signatures for images and Helm chart artifacts before promotion to production registries.
- Typical sign flow for CI runner:
  - generate image at CI, push to staging repo with tag sha256:...
  - cosign sign --key k8s://... <registry>/redwood-inference/model-server@sha256:...
  - upload signature and predicate (in-toto or simple predicate) to artifact-bucket under artifact-bundle/<version>/
- For Helm charts we attach a provenance file (.prov) and cosign-sign the chart tarball.
- If customer uses an HSM, pipeline must produce an attestable key reference and sign with remote signer API; record signer key thumbprint in release notes.

Terraform module interactions (common pitfalls):
- module versions pinned with exact git tags in the control-plane repo. Avoid floating branches in release PRs.
- When the TF module introduces new IAM roles for the operator, include a separate PR that applies the IAM change first in a maintenance window (apply -> wait -> rollout).
- State lock overlaps: CI runners must acquire state locks when running terraform plan/apply in automation. If multiple automation lanes touch the same state, add a queue or use tf-lock service.

Argo/GitOps rollout sequencing (recommended pattern):
1) Promote artifact-bundle to staging registry and update kustomize overlay (control-plane) with new image digests and chart ref
2) Create argocd Application change in a canary overlay (namespace: canary-<release>)
3) Argo deploys canary App; run automated acceptance tests against canary (see smoke test section)
4) If acceptance passes, patch main overlay to point to same artifact and let Argo sync (or use progressive sync via Argo Rollouts)
Notes: keep canary lifecycle short (10–30 minutes) and automated. Manual approvals add latency; strongly prefer automated gates backed by SLO checks.

Smoke tests and automated acceptance (scripts we run):
- smoke/health.sh <cluster> <namespace> — checks pod readiness, probes, KV cache health endpoints
- smoke/api-latency.py — runs representative inference requests and records p50/p95/p99
- smoke/regression-prompt-suite.yaml — small prompt set to detect hallucination/regressions at a high level
Gate thresholds (defaults):
- p95 latency not > 1.5x baseline
- error rate < 0.1% over test window
- key metric: cache hit rate within 5% of baseline
If any threshold fails -> automatic rollback trigger (see Rollback section).

Rollback mechanics (fast path):
1) Argo sync previous revision for the Application (argocd app rollback <app> --to-revision <rev>) or apply previous kustomize overlay commit
2) Revert Terraform if TF changes were part of release (only for non-breaking infra changes). For network/IAM changes open immediate INF ticket and escalate to oncall infra.
3) Revoke compromised artifacts: tag vulnerable image as deprecated and add deny rule in repository (if supported).
4) Notify stakeholders via #private-deploys and create a postmortem if incident severity >= P2

Verification checklist post-rollback:
- All Apps in k8s are at expected revision and healthy
- Inference p95/p99 back to pre-release baselines
- No new CrashLoopBackoffs or OOMKills since rollback time
- Terraform state consistent, no partial resources left behind

Telemetry & observability checks to include in gate: (queries to attach to pipeline)
- Prometheus: sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (code)
- Latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))
- Error spikes: increase in 5xx responses > 3x baseline => fail gate
- Cost guard: unusual token generation increase (>200% of baseline) => alert but do not block automatically (ops review)

Template Helm values snippet for canary overlay (example):
# canary-values.yaml
replicaCount: 2
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 500m
    memory: 2Gi
image:
  repository: registry.staging.redwood-inference/private-model-server
  tag: sha256-<digest>
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
args:
  model_variant: "offload-quantized"

Commands (cheat sheet):
- preview Argo manifest: kustomize build overlays/canary | kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f -
- sync Argo app: argocd app sync private-model-server-canary
- rollback: argocd app rollback private-model-server --to-revision 3
- sign image locally: cosign sign --key $COSIGN_KEY <image>@sha256:<digest>

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical location for storing attestations for onprem (object store vs registry-based predicate). Customer-specific tradeoffs exist.
- Improve TF module test coverage for drift scenarios (write unit/integration tests in infra repo).
- Add automated chart provenance verification in Argo pre-sync hook (prototype using cosign).

Post-release runbook (first 2 hours):
- 0-15m: confirm Argo reports all apps Healthy and Synced
- 15-30m: run smoke suite and latency tests, compare to baseline
- 30-60m: run expanded traffic tests at 20% of production load (canary routing)
- 60-120m: escalate if any anomalies or continue gradual promotion to 100%

Notes from past incidents (lessons learned):
- INF-1982: missed SBOM attachment led to delayed rollback; fixed by adding SBOM required check in CI gating step
- INF-2401: TF apply that modified node IAM during rollout caused pod scheduling failures — now split infra changes into separate maintenance PRs

Appendix: quick TF module pattern (recommended):
- module/*/main.tf keeps resources minimal and returns outputs: operator_role_arn, registry_policy_id
- Control-plane uses remote state data source to read outputs, not copy them into overlays
- When adding new module inputs, bump module major version and cut a release tag to avoid accidental auto-upgrades

If you're running a hands-on upgrade for a customer, copy this doc into the customer folder and edit the canary thresholds and registry endpoints. Keep a brief audit trail in the release PR with links to the smoke run logs and argocd sync history.

Contacts:
- oncall-infra: paged via PagerDuty (see ops@redwood-inference)
- release-coordinator: Miguel Ortega

Last notes: this is intentionally concise and operational — feel free to add small customer-specific sections under the control-plane repo. We'll iterate the automated gates as we run more onprem upgrades next quarter.
